output.impression: Neuropsychological evaluation demonstrates a predominantly amnestic profile with multi-domain involvement. Episodic memory is severely impaired: RAVLT immediate recall at the 3rd percentile, delayed recall at the 1st percentile and recognition at the 2nd percentile indicate a storage-type deficit with poor encoding. Semantic fluency (Category Fluency, Animals, 8th percentile) and confrontation naming (Boston Naming Test, 18th percentile) are impaired. Letter fluency (FAS, 22nd percentile) and executive function (Trail Making B, 15th percentile) are mildly reduced. Visuoconstructive ability (Rey Complex Figure Copy, 30th percentile) and processing speed (Trail Making A, 28th percentile) are within the low-normal range. Screening scores: MMSE 21/30, MoCA 17/30. Mood screening is borderline (GDS 5/15); cognitive deficits are disproportionate to any mood contribution. Multi-domain cognitive impairment with amnestic predominance, at a level consistent with mild dementia given the reported functional decline.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure 14 cmH2O. WBC 2 cells/uL (lymphocytes), RBC 0. Protein 42 mg/dL, glucose 68 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.61), all within reference ranges. Decreased Abeta42 (362 pg/mL) and Abeta42/40 ratio (0.046) with elevated p-tau181 (84 pg/mL) and total tau (512 pg/mL). This biomarker profile is consistent with Alzheimer disease pathology. Clinical correlation recommended.

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to donepezil or piperidine derivatives; the documented sulfonamide allergy does not cross-react
interactions: Donepezil + Amlodipine: no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction; amlodipine does not lower the heart rate.
Donepezil + Aspirin 81 mg: cholinesterase inhibitors increase gastric acid secretion; with aspirin, monitor for dyspepsia and gastrointestinal bleeding.
Donepezil + Tamsulosin: no pharmacokinetic interaction; additive risk of dizziness and syncope (orthostatic hypotension with tamsulosin, vagotonic effect of donepezil).
Donepezil + Metformin: no clinically significant interaction; both commonly cause nausea and diarrhea at initiation.
Donepezil + Rosuvastatin: no clinically significant interaction.
output.proposed: Donepezil 5 mg once daily, increasing to 10 mg after 4 to 6 weeks if tolerated
warnings: Vagotonic effect: bradycardia, heart block and syncope can occur; check pulse before starting and at titration (resting heart rate 72/min recorded at this visit)
Cholinomimetics may cause bladder outflow obstruction; benign prostatic hyperplasia on tamsulosin: ask about urinary retention
Gastrointestinal effects (nausea, diarrhea, anorexia, weight loss) are common during titration and usually transient
Concurrent anticholinergic drugs oppose the effect of cholinesterase inhibitors

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MMSE 21/30 with amnestic-predominant impairment not helped by cueing and informant-confirmed decline over about three years; instrumental independence lost (finances taken over, driving and cooking supervised), placing the syndrome at mild dementia
action_criteria.label: Perform a structured cognitive and behavioural assessment with informant history: a validated bedside instrument with the per-domain breakdown, whether delayed recall improves with cueing, and an explicit account of which instrumental activities have been lost. The syndrome must be documented before it is attributed
action_criteria.rationale: Whether this is mild cognitive impairment or dementia is decided clinically, by a validated instrument and the family's account of instrumental function, before any biomarker is interpreted [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amnestic profile with disproportionate impairment of delayed recall and limited benefit from cueing, plus involvement of at least one other cognitive domain
action_criteria.label: Order comprehensive neuropsychological testing to characterize the cognitive profile and establish a baseline for tracking
action_criteria.rationale: Formal testing defines the domains involved beyond the bedside screen, weighs the borderline mood score against the memory deficit, and sets a baseline for follow-up [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal TSH, B12 310 pg/mL with normal homocysteine and folate, non-reactive RPR and negative HIV: no reversible contributor; glucose 112 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.4% on metformin
action_criteria.label: Order the cognitive laboratory panel to identify reversible or contributing causes
action_criteria.rationale: Thyroid dysfunction, B12 deficiency (he takes metformin), syphilis, HIV and metabolic derangement are treatable contributors that must be excluded before the decline is attributed to a neurodegenerative cause [AAN_dementia_2018].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral hippocampal atrophy (Scheltens MTA 3 right, 2-3 left) with temporoparietal cortical volume loss; Evans index 0.33 with proportionate sulcal widening and no DESH; Fazekas 1-2 white matter change without infarct
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI with dementia (volumetric) protocol to assess medial-temporal atrophy and exclude vascular disease, hippocampal sclerosis, NPH, and mass lesions
action_criteria.rationale: Structural MRI excludes vascular, mass and hydrocephalic causes of the decline (his gait is mildly slow) and shows whether the atrophy pattern supports Alzheimer disease [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positivity: decreased CSF Abeta42/40 ratio with raised p-tau181 and total tau, or a positive amyloid PET
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET when the result would change management
action_criteria.rationale: Either CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau or amyloid PET establishes amyloid status; one conclusive test is enough, and it is needed when the diagnosis remains uncertain after the clinical, neuropsychological and MRI assessment or when disease-modifying treatment is being considered [NIA_AA_2018] [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction needing a dose change; counselling on gastrointestinal bleeding with aspirin, bladder outflow symptoms with BPH, vagotonic bradycardia and syncope
action_criteria.label: Check donepezil against his current medicines before starting it
action_criteria.rationale: A cholinesterase inhibitor is offered for mild Alzheimer dementia; aspirin, tamsulosin with benign prostatic hyperplasia, amlodipine, metformin and rosuvastatin are reviewed first, although none is a contraindication [NICE_NG97].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat his back pain or urinary symptoms with anticholinergic drugs (amitriptyline or other tricyclics, oxybutynin, tolterodine); anticholinergic burden worsens cognition and opposes a cholinesterase inhibitor [Beers_2023].
Do not attribute the decline to depression; a GDS of 5/15 and feeling 'useless' do not explain a storage-type amnestic deficit with loss of instrumental function.
Do not start memantine at the mild dementia stage; it is for moderate or severe Alzheimer disease or when cholinesterase inhibitors are not tolerated [NICE_NG97].
required_recommendations: Disclose the diagnosis of mild Alzheimer dementia to him, his wife and son, and discuss prognosis, advance care planning, durable power of attorney and carer support [NICE_NG97].
Advise him not to drive until a formal driving assessment, given the disorientation on a familiar route and his family's concern, and follow local licensing rules.
Address home and medicine safety: keep cooking supervised after the stove was left on twice, keep the finances with his wife, and have his wife supervise his medicines and appointments.

Offer a trial of a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine or galantamine) for mild Alzheimer dementia after checking pulse, conduction history and current medicines, with attention to gastrointestinal bleeding on aspirin and urinary retention with benign prostatic hyperplasia [NICE_NG97].

Offer amyloid biomarker testing (CSF or amyloid PET) if a biological diagnosis would change management, such as eligibility for anti-amyloid treatment or diagnostic uncertainty; one conclusive test is sufficient [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].
Continue vascular risk management (blood pressure, diabetes with HbA1c 6.4% on metformin, statin) and encourage a return to daily walking.

avoided_actions.rationale: ECG is unrelated to the dementia workup; no cardiac symptom or syncope to justify it in this case
Echocardiography is unrelated to the dementia workup; no cardioembolic indication in this presentation
Cardiac monitoring is not indicated; no arrhythmia, syncope, or palpitations described
Head CT adds little when MRI is available; MRI is the preferred structural modality for dementia workup

differential.key_features: No visual hallucinations, cognitive fluctuations or dream enactment, and no rigidity, tremor or bradykinesia; the mildly slow gait is not parkinsonian and the profile is amnestic with preserved visuoconstruction on formal testing

No disinhibition, personality change, compulsions or hyperorality; word-finding pauses with intact repetition and comprehension do not meet a primary progressive aphasia syndrome; amnestic profile with temporoparietal-predominant atrophy, and Alzheimer biomarkers when obtained

Diabetes, hypertension and Fazekas 1-2 white matter change give a vascular risk background, but there is no infarct and the course is gradual rather than stepwise; small vessel disease may contribute but does not explain the amnestic profile with marked hippocampal atrophy
Insidious course over months to years with disproportionate delayed-recall impairment and limited benefit from cueing is not typical of pseudodementia

differential.diagnosis: Reversible metabolic, endocrine, or sleep-related cognitive impairment
differential.key_features: TSH, B12 (310 pg/mL with normal homocysteine), folate, RPR and HIV are normal; no snoring or sleep disturbance reported; the progressive amnestic decline is not explained by any of these

Evans index 0.33 and a mildly slow gait raise it, but the ventricles are proportionate to sulcal widening without DESH, the gait has a normal base and no magnetic quality, there is no urinary incontinence, and the cognitive profile is cortical amnestic

key_clinical_evidence: Probable Alzheimer disease dementia is a clinical diagnosis under NIA-AA 2011: insidious onset, informant-confirmed progression, an amnestic presentation with another domain affected, and decline in usual activities; hippocampal and temporoparietal atrophy on MRI support it but are not required [NIA_AA_2011]
The hallmark cognitive feature of AD is impaired delayed recall with rapid forgetting and limited benefit from cueing, reflecting a storage-type (hippocampal) memory deficit

Ventricular enlargement with an Evans index above 0.3 is common with atrophy; proportionate sulcal widening without DESH, a non-magnetic gait and no incontinence argue for ex vacuo dilatation rather than normal pressure hydrocephalus
Cholinesterase inhibitors are indicated for mild to moderate Alzheimer dementia; memantine is for moderate or severe disease or when cholinesterase inhibitors are not tolerated [NICE_NG97]

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Ventricular enlargement is proportionate to cortical atrophy without DESH, the gait has a normal base without magnetic quality, and there is no urinary incontinence; ex vacuo dilatation in Alzheimer disease

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Kenji Takahashi is a 76-year-old right-handed retired civil engineer who is brought to the outpatient neurology clinic by his wife and eldest son for evaluation of progressive memory difficulties. His wife reports that she first noticed subtle changes approximately three years ago, when her husband began asking the same questions repeatedly within the span of a few minutes, something he had never done before. He would forget conversations they had had earlier in the day and occasionally could not recall visits from their grandchildren just days later. Over the past year, the symptoms have become substantially more apparent. He has missed several scheduled medical appointments despite previously being very organized and punctual throughout his career. His wife took over managing the household finances approximately eight months ago after discovering that he had paid the same utility bill twice and left another bill unpaid for two months, tasks he had always handled meticulously as an engineer. He has become less engaged in his longtime hobby of building model railroads, leaving a project half-finished in the garage for the past four months, which his son describes as very uncharacteristic. On several occasions, he has placed items in unusual locations, such as putting his reading glasses in the refrigerator and his wallet in a kitchen drawer rather than the entry table where he had kept it for decades. His wife has also noticed word-finding difficulties; he sometimes substitutes a general word like 'thing' for specific objects during conversation, though he seems aware of these lapses and becomes frustrated. Three months ago, he became briefly disoriented while driving to a familiar shopping center he has visited for over twenty years, taking a wrong turn and needing to pull over to reorient himself. Since then, his wife has been accompanying him on all drives, and his son has raised the question of whether he should continue driving. He continues to dress, bathe, and groom himself independently and manages basic meal preparation, though his wife now supervises cooking after he left the gas stove on twice without a pot. His sleep has been generally unremarkable; his wife does not report any episodes of acting out dreams, shouting, or movements during sleep. He denies persistent sadness but admits to feeling 'useless' at times when he cannot remember things. He denies visual hallucinations, paranoid ideation, personality changes, or aggressive behavior. There has been no tremor, falls, or incontinence. His appetite has been normal and his weight has been stable.

neurological_exam.additional: No paratonic rigidity. No grasp reflex. No myoclonus. No primitive reflexes (palmomental, glabellar tap negative). Anosmia not formally tested.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing normal bilaterally. No dysmetria. Rapid alternating movements intact.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, reactive to light bilaterally (right pseudophakic). Extraocular movements full, no nystagmus. Visual fields full to confrontation. Facial sensation intact to light touch V1-V3 bilaterally. Face symmetric at rest and with activation. Hearing grossly intact bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline, no fasciculations.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly slow but steady gait. Normal base width. Slightly shortened stride length. Tandem gait performed with minor difficulty. Romberg negative. Able to rise from chair without using arms.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person and place; knows the year and the season but cannot state the month, the exact date or the day of the week. MMSE 21/30, losing points on recall (0/3 at 5 minutes), orientation (3 points lost), attention/serial sevens (2 errors), and copy of intersecting pentagons (mildly distorted). Clock drawing test shows numbers clustered on the right side with hands placed at an incorrect time. Spontaneous speech is fluent but pauses frequently to search for words. Able to name common objects but has difficulty with low-frequency items. Repetition intact. Follows simple two-step commands but has difficulty with complex three-step instructions.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk and tone in all extremities. No rigidity or cogwheeling. Strength 5/5 throughout upper and lower extremities bilaterally. No pronator drift. No tremor or involuntary movements.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffman sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, and temperature in all extremities. Vibration sense mildly diminished at bilateral great toes (age-appropriate). Proprioception intact.
